name: _BoundedLines

    the stream once `limit` bytes have been taken, so a trickle of well-formed
    small deltas cannot either. `truncated` records that the ceiling bound, so
    the caller can say so instead of returning a cut-off answer that reads as
    complete.

name: _writer
docstring:

    codepage (cp1252, cp437, ...), and writing raw UTF-8 bytes straight to
    the buffer bypasses `TextIOWrapper`'s console translation, producing
    mojibake even though no exception is raised (#169). A non-ASCII token
    from a model would otherwise abort the whole answer mid-sentence, so the
    chunk is folded to what the stream's own encoding can represent first.

docstring:
NaN compares False against every relational operator in IEEE 754.

    `float("nan") + CLOCK_SKEW < now` is False, so a naive expiry check lets a
    NaN `exp` claim through as if the token never expires. It must fail closed.

    `key["n"]` on a key set that never published one is a KeyError, and a
    KeyError is not an AuthError -- it becomes a 500 on the tool path and a
    dead handler thread on the refusal path, which catches AuthError only.

    `str()` of a JSON integer is a run of decimal digits, which base64url
    either decodes to some unrelated modulus or rejects as bad padding. Either
    way the key is silently reinterpreted rather than refused, so the type
    check matters as much as the presence check.

    real shape, not a hypothetical one.

name: test_a_jwk_whose_key_ops_excludes_verify_is_refused
docstring: RFC 7517 §4.3: an explicit op list that omits "verify" forbids verifying.

name: test_a_jwk_declaring_neither_use_nor_key_ops_still_verifies
docstring:
Absent means unconstrained, per RFC 7517 §4.2/§4.3.

    This is the ordinary JWKS entry that every real issuer serves, and a
    purpose check that reads "absent" as "forbidden" would lock out all of
    them. Pinned as its own case because the two rejections above pass just as
    happily under a check that rejects everything.

docstring: The positive declaration is honoured, not merely tolerated.

name: test_an_expired_ttl_refetches
docstring:
Keys are re-read once the TTL has elapsed.

    The clock is injected rather than slept through. An earlier version used
    ttl=0.0 and two back-to-back calls, which passes only if the monotonic
    clock ticks between them -- so it passed on one machine and failed on
    another, where Windows falls back to GetTickCount64's ~15.6ms granularity
    and both calls read the same instant.

name: test_a_zero_ttl_never_caches
docstring:
`ttl=0` means "do not cache", whatever the clock's resolution.

    With a strict `>` comparison this promise silently depended on the clock
    ticking between calls, which is exactly the flake above in its other form:
    a configuration that says "never cache" would keep serving stale keys.

    it. A TypeError is not an AuthError, so the transport's refusal path never
    sees it: the handler thread dies and the caller gets no response at all,
    not a 401 and not a 500. Only AuthError is an acceptable outcome here.

name: test_iss197_a_withheld_request_body_is_answered_rather_than_waited_on
docstring:
Issue 197: headers promising a megabyte, then silence.

    Without a handler `timeout`, socketserver never arms settimeout() and
    `rfile.read(Content-Length)` blocks for as long as the client cares to hold
    the socket -- one pinned thread per connection, on a server that caps
    neither. The shipped 30s is far too long to sit through here, so the test
    pins the attribute's existence separately and then shrinks it to prove the
    second half: that the read failing becomes a 408 rather than a handler
    thread dying with the client still waiting.

name: AbortingWriter
docstring:

    The real shape is a client that hangs up mid-response, which Windows
    reports as ConnectionAbortedError -- the sibling of BrokenPipeError and
    ConnectionResetError that the old guard did not name. Forcing it beats
    racing a real socket close, which lands on a different write every run.

    Write 1 is the header flush from `end_headers()`; write 2 is the body.

name: test_iss199_a_disconnect_during_a_response_reaches_no_error_reporter
docstring:
Issue 199: a client that hangs up mid-response is not an error.

    `_send_json` guarded only the body write and only two of ConnectionError's
    three subclasses, so a disconnect at `end_headers()` (every platform) or a
    ConnectionAbortedError at the body write (Windows) escaped into the
    server's error reporter. Either way the operator gets a record for
    something that is not a fault, and before this package owned that reporter
    the record was a multi-line traceback in a stream promised to be JSON-lines.

name: test_iss199_an_escaping_handler_error_is_one_json_line

    socketserver's default `handle_error` prints a dashed banner plus a full
    traceback to stderr, which `events.py` promises is one JSON object per
    line. A SIEM parsing it line by line gets a dozen lines that parse as none,
    at exactly the moment the record matters most.

name: test_iss233_a_deeply_nested_json_body_is_a_clean_400

    ~40 KB of nesting is well inside MAX_BODY_BYTES, and this runs before
    `authenticate()`, so any caller that can reach POST /mcp could kill a
    handler thread outright on a server that is otherwise fully locked down.

name: test_iss243_a_crlf_in_the_oidc_issuer_cannot_inject_a_response_header

    rule for header values and this path did not follow it. The fix is
    structural: `_send_json` sanitises every extra header, so the rule holds
    for call sites nobody has written yet.

name: test_iss249_a_chunked_request_body_is_refused_with_411

    A chunked body measured as zero bytes was never read, so a spec-legal
    client got "expected a JSON-RPC object" and a socket still holding its
    request. Refusing the encoding by name says what is actually wrong.

name: test_iss249_the_handler_pins_its_protocol_version_deliberately

    It is also the base class's default, so only the presence of the attribute
    on this class distinguishes "chosen" from "never thought about" -- and the
    choice is what keeps an unread request body (a refused Transfer-Encoding, a
    413'd Content-Length, a read that timed out part-way) from being left in a
    socket that the next request would be parsed out of.

docstring:
The per-record disk sync is a flag, and it is off unless asked for.

    ISS-244 made `_LockedAppender.write` flush rather than fsync, because the
    sync was taken while holding both the thread lock and the OS-level file
    lock -- on the threaded HTTP transport that serialised every request behind
    a disk sync, and stderr already carries every record. Durability for the
    file copy is still available; it just has to be chosen. The default is the
    half worth pinning: a config that quietly went back to syncing would
    reintroduce the throughput ceiling with nothing failing.

docstring:
The schema is the whole contract, and it has two fields.

    Labels stay path- and size-derived: `detectType`, `detectAreas` and
    `calculateSize` are exact, and a model guess that contradicted them would
    make a label mean "computed" on some PRs and "guessed" on others with
    nothing in the comment to say which. Review, risk assessment and anything
    requiring knowledge of code outside the diff are out of scope by
    construction -- there is no field to put them in.

    Feeding AGENTS.md (or any repo content) to the model is what turns a
    description into a review, which is the thing this bot deliberately does
    not do. The rule checklist in the comment stays where it was: derived from

    confidence 1.0: tier 1 declines a self-target and tier 2 -- which now
    *includes* the caller -- prices both readings at 1/n.

    `[c.to_dict() for c in self.checks]`, which an earlier version of this fix
    resolved to `Rep

publish.yml passes this list to `--files`. A path `rewrite()` touches but
    the list omits produces a release commit that bumps some surfaces and not
    others, on a tag PyPI will not let you reuse.

name: test_files_mode_prints_exactly_those_paths
docstring:
The `--files` CLI is what publish.yml shells out to; if its output stops
    being a plain space-separated list, `read -ra` silently builds the wrong
    array.

name: test_every_surface_path_exists
docstring:
A renamed doc silently drops its surface from both the bump and the
    check, so the table naming a file that is gone must fail loudly.

name: test_bump_moves_every_surface_to_the_new_version
docstring: The whole point: after a bump, nothing still reads the old version.

name: test_bump_rewrites_the_documented_major_tag
docstring:
Named separately because it is the surface that was missed. `@v9` and
    "every 9.x release", hand-derived from a 9.9.9 target.

name: _rewrite_in_sandbox
signature: def _rewrite_in_sandbox(tmp_path: Path, version: str) -> dict[str, str]:
docstring:
Run `rewrite(version)` against copies, never the real checkout.

    `version_surfaces.ROOT` is module state, so it is swapped for the duration
    and restored -- a test that bumped the working tree and failed halfway would
    leave the repo claiming a version it never released.

name: test_the_sandbox_helper_leaves_the_real_tree_alone
docstring:
The guard on the guard: if `_rewrite_in_sandbox` ever edited the checkout,
    every other test here would still pass while corrupting the repo.

name: test_major_surfaces_carry_only_the_major
docstring:
`kind="major"` exists because publish.yml's floating tag is `vN`. If a
    major surface started expecting a full version, every bump would write
    `@v2.1.0` into a `uses:` line and point users at a tag that does not move.

name: FakeGraph
docstring: The three attributes `write_html` reads off a Graph.

name: render
docstring: Write a page for a graph called `name` and hand back its HTML.

name: chrome
docstring: The two HTML contexts the repo name is interpolated into.

name: test_a_script_tag_in_the_repo_name_is_escaped
docstring: A repo literally named `<script>alert(1)</script>` must not execute.

name: test_attribute_and_tag_breakouts_in_the_repo_name_are_escaped
docstring: Neither the <title> nor the <h1> may be escaped out of.

name: test_the_data_placeholder_in_a_repo_name_is_not_expanded
docstring:
A repo named `__R2G_DATA__` must not pull the JSON payload into <h1>.

    The template is filled by a single regex pass over both placeholders, so a
    replacement's *output* is never rescanned. A naive sequence of `.replace`
    calls -- title first, then data -- would substitute the whole graph payload
    into the title and the heading.

name: test_the_payload_placeholder_still_receives_the_real_data
docstring: The single-pass guard must not break the substitution it protects.

name: test_angle_brackets_in_the_payload_cannot_close_the_script_block
docstring: `</script>` inside indexed content must not terminate the block early.

name: test_viz_nodes_zero_renders_no_nodes
docstring: 0 means an empty graph, not every node.

name: test_viz_nodes_none_is_the_no_cap_spelling
docstring: `all` on the CLI arrives here as None and keeps every node.

name: test_the_settle_loop_is_incremental_not_a_blocking_while
docstring:
Layout must yield to the browser between batches.

    A synchronous `while (alpha > ...) step()` blocks the main thread for the
    whole settle: no paint, no input, no scroll. Bounding the iteration count
    bounds the freeze but does not remove it.

name: test_the_iteration_cap_is_configurable_from_the_container
docstring: maxIterations defaults to 500 and is overridable per page.

name: test_a_progress_indicator_exists_and_is_hidden_when_idle
docstring: The user must be able to tell a laying-out page from a frozen one.

name: test_pointer_capture_is_released_on_both_pointerup_and_pointercancel
docstring:
A capture never released swallows every later pointer event on the page.

    This is a source-level assertion rather than a DOM test: a real one needs a
    JS runtime (jsdom or playwright), and this repo has no Node toolchain in its
    dev extra. It pins the property that actually regressed -- a handler losing
    its release call -- but it cannot prove the released id matches the captured
    one. Noted in DONE.md as the one untested-in-a-browser property here.

name: test_pointer_capture_release_is_guarded
docstring: releasePointerCapture throws if the element does not hold the capture.

name: test_the_page_is_self_contained
docstring: No network at render time and none at view time: one file, no fetches.

name: test_payload_is_valid_json
docstring: Whatever escaping is applied, the blob must still parse.

name: test_search_focus_and_legend_ui_are_present
docstring:
Presence check for the search box, focus mode and the legend panel.

    Not a browser test (this repo has no Node/jsdom toolchain in its dev
    extra, same limitation noted for the pointer-capture tests above) -- just
    confirms the three new pieces of UI actually landed in the rendered page
    and in TEMPLATE's script, rather than a full DOM/interaction check.
